### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/dashboard.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via DashboardSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via DashboardSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/dashboard.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `443c399d2a49e4cd4cda4c9447ff5cee55c7689c` — the merge of head `1b39eebd716d95164adb38b5f508b8390edbc5f5` into base `ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 443c399d2a49e4cd4cda4c9447ff5cee55c7689c && git checkout 443c399d2a49e4cd4cda4c9447ff5cee55c7689c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd 1b39eebd716d95164adb38b5f508b8390edbc5f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd && git merge --no-ff 1b39eebd716d95164adb38b5f508b8390edbc5f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af81d59c30a3c4100d7a595bf213d0a5d7aa50a1`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22611 (body; comments 6094878821, 6095014058, 6095248235, 6096250858), card #22639 (body; comments 6095327925, 6096254862), PR #22665 (body, file list, the one bot comment), the net diff `3d0eeefa4a..af81d59c30` (18 files, +346/−4), the tree at the head read through git objects, and the check-runs on the head polled at 09:52Z, 09:53Z, 09:56Z and once more before this post. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The two keys, one shape — right.** `requiredPermissions: z.array(z.string()).optional().describe(AUDIENCE_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION)` on `ListViewShapeSchema` (`view.zod.ts:2910`) and on `DashboardSchema` (`dashboard.zod.ts:1808`), no default. Identical in shape to every other carrier at this head: `AppSchema` (`app.zod.ts:1593`), the navigation item (`app.zod.ts:364`), `ActionSchema` (`action.zod.ts:1536`) and the four record blocks (`component.zod.ts:1484/1624/1729/2179`). The new test holds the two declarations byte-identical to each other and shape-identical to the app's (describe stripped), and refuses a string, a non-string member and `{ anyOf: [...] }` as `invalid_type` at the key, never `unrecognized_keys`.

**Every door that now accepts the key, named — right, and the generated references agree.** Declared on the shape, so it reaches: `ListViewSchema` (`ListViewShapeSchema` plus bindings, `:3131`); `ObjectListViewSchema` (`ListViewShapeSchema.omit({ userFilters })`, `:4882`); the view container's `list` and `listViews[string]` (`:4978`); an object's own `listViews[string]` (`object.zod.ts:2515`); the view item's `config` on the `list` arm, and its wire twin; the `GetUiViewResponse` `list` / `listViews[string]` bodies; and `ListViewOverlayWireSchema` (`:6384`, the `PUT /api/v1/meta/view` runtime write door — the one with no reference table). That is the 10 generated rows in the diff, one per table: `ui/view.mdx` ×6 (ListView, ObjectListView, View.list, View.listViews[string], ViewItem[list].config, ViewItemWire[list].config), `api/protocol.mdx` ×2 (GetUiViewResponse.list, .listViews[string]), `data/object.mdx` ×1 (Object.listViews[string]), `ui/dashboard.mdx` ×1. `authorable-surface/ui.json` gains exactly the three schema-level entries (`ui/Dashboard`, `ui/ListView`, `ui/ObjectListView`). Declaring it on `ListViewSchema` instead would have left `ObjectListViewSchema` without it — the third list-view shape the ruling did not take.

**Declared-is-enforced in the window before #22639 — every describe sentence is true at this head.**
- "No server reads this key today": a grep of every non-test source under `packages/` at the head finds `requiredPermissions` read only for an app and its navigation entries (`rest/meta-item-read-gate.ts:740,757`, `runtime/domains/meta.ts`), an action (`runtime/action-execution.ts:468`, `rest/rest-server.ts:1640`), a field (`metadata-core` FLS, `objectql/search-companion.ts:137`) and an object. No read under `view`, `dashboard` or `listViews` anywhere in `rest`, `runtime`, `metadata-core`, `objectql` or the plugins. The objectui half of that claim (pin `20c6d351ad74`, which is `.objectui-sha` at the head) is the dev's and the seat's measurement; this record carries it as accepted, not re-measured.
- "names that permission sets grant through `systemPermissions`": `PermissionSetSchema.systemPermissions` (`permission.zod.ts:880`). "ALL hold": the app arm's `every`. "Absent or empty: no audience gate": pinned (absent stays absent, `[]` parses).
- `[ADR-0066]` exists (`docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md`); the bare marker without a D-number is the record-block precedent already on `main`. `[PLANNED — not enforced yet]` is the machine-read marker: `check-liveness.mts` `markerStatus` tests the `planned` regex before the `experimental` one, so the clause's "not enforced" does not misgrade it — and both rows exist, so the ledger status governs anyway.

**Liveness rows per `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` — right.** Both rows are `status: planned`, `verifiedAt: 2026-10-10` (today, not future-dated), `authorWarn: true`, a tracker-free `authorHint` that does not say "Remove it", and a maintainer `note` naming the carrier (#22639) and the exact flip (cite the gate, drop `authorWarn`/`authorHint`, delete the describe clause). The README's table is "`planned` warns only with `authorWarn: true`" and rule 2 (no materialised default — none here) — both satisfied. The rows sit at `view.props.list.children.requiredPermissions` (one drill level, inside what the lint flattens) and `dashboard.props.requiredPermissions`. The regenerated `state-counts/` shards move view 89 → 90 and dashboard 55 → 56 with `planned` 0 → 1 on each, and the hand-written README cells say "this type's only `planned` row" — true against the generated counts. The `Spec property liveness` check-run (the `check:liveness` gate) is green on this head.

**Does the lint reach what the rows say — yes, exactly.** `loadWarnMap` keys the warn map `list.requiredPermissions` (view) and `requiredPermissions` (dashboard); `TYPE_COLLECTIONS` lists `views` and `dashboards`; `getNested` resolves `item.list.requiredPermissions`. `listViews` is a top-level `live` row with no `children` in `view.json`, so a container's named entries are not walked, and an object's `listViews` is reached by no walk (the object walk reads `object.json` rows only). Each note says precisely that, and the describe clause is the channel for those doors. The lint pin (`lint-liveness-properties.test.ts`) reads the two shipped rows, asserts the rule id and the row's own hint, and has a lit control beside each quiet one. One observation, no action: on an authored EMPTY list the two paths differ — `[item.requiredPermissions]` counts `[]` as authored (a dashboard warns), while `getNested` flattens `[]` to nothing (a view's `list` stays silent). The describe says empty is no gate, so the dashboard over-warns on a value that does nothing; harmless.

**No any-of form, no alias, `sharing` untouched — right.** The any-of object is refused and pinned. No alias fold on either schema names the key (the `permissions`/`requiredCapabilities` folds at this head are the field, action, app and bulk-action tables only). `sharing: ViewSharingSchema.optional()` appears in the diff as a context line only.

**`capabilities.mdx` — true at this head.** "An app, a navigation item, an action, a record block, and a list view or a dashboard — everywhere a list of names the user must all hold": each named carrier is `string[]` and AND-ed (the record block's describe says "must ALL hold", presentation-only). The paragraph scopes itself to entries; objects and fields also carry the key (an object's may be a per-operation map) and are the page's own station ⑤, so the sentence is not falsified. The example parses by the page's own precedent: `capabilities: [defineCapability(...)]` (`stack.zod.ts:501`, `capabilities.ts:217`) and `permissions: [{ name, systemPermissions }]` (`stack.zod.ts:486`). The callout is true (no reader). The directory is hand-written prose in the regen ledger (only `system-context.mdx` is routed), so a hand edit is the right act; the section carries no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` scans `content/`).

**Generated references, authorable surface, reconciliation omit rows against the gates.** The two `omit` rows follow the `object.externalSharingModel` precedent word for word in kind; the object-rooted `dashboard` row is required by the test, the union-rooted `view` row is symmetry. `authorable-surface.base.json`, `json-schema.manifest/**` and the gitignored `json-schema/` tree are `gen:schema` artifacts adjudicated by `check:authorable-surface`; the metadata-forms i18n bundles derive from form rows, and none was added. Concluded green on this head: `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs`, `Build Core` (hosts `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` (`check:type-check-debt`), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 2/6 and 6/6, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, the three claim guards, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1/3–3/3 and its gate, `Temporal Conformance`. Skipped by design: `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`. STILL RUNNING at the last poll before this post, and therefore not judged here: `Lint & Repo Gates` (hosts `check:generated --reconcile-only`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, ESLint), `Test Core` 1/6, 3/6, 4/6 and 5/6 (the spec and lint suites, so the 89 + 3 new pins). The verdict below rests on the concluded set; a red on any of the running jobs is a red the required-status rules refuse on their own, and this record does not pre-clear it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` — right. Two published schemas accept a key they refused before (`unrecognized_keys`); every document that parsed before parses the same; the exported `ListView`/`Dashboard` types gain an optional property. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the well-formed declaration for that (AGENTS.md: `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(widening)` is the non-breaking arm), present in both the changeset body and the PR body; `Check Changeset` is green. `AUDIENCE_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION` is not re-exported from `ui/index.ts` or `src/index.ts`, so no new published export and no `api-surface` row — consistent with the diff.

`@objectstack/lint` publishes nothing here — right. Its only change is `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts`; the package's `files` are `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, so the test reaches no tarball and no changeset is owed. No other released package is touched. The changeset names #22639 in prose: `check:doc-authoring`'s roots are `.claude`, `docs`, `skills`, `content`, and at least eight existing `.changeset/*.md` cite issue numbers — precedent, not a defect.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Refused PR-assignee write** (ACCEPT deviation 1): the PR has no assignee and is still `draft: true`. Not a contract matter; left to the maintainer, as the ACCEPT states. This record does not flip the draft.
2. **`check:type-check-debt --re-measure` ran a whole-workspace build** (deviation 2): a process breach the dev disclosed and did not re-measure locally. Both gates it forbade locally are now measured by CI on this head: `Type Check · debt ledger` success, `Build Core` (with `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) success. Resolved on evidence. The hazard — a derived gate that launches `turbo run build` under concurrent devs — is the seat's to carry; outside this record.
3. **File surface beyond the claim** (deviation 3): the two reconciliation `omit` rows (required for the object-rooted `dashboard`), the lint pin in `packages/lint` (the claim said pins in `packages/spec`; the repo's real-ledger pattern pins an `authorWarn` row in the lint, and that pin is the tripwire that turns red at the flip), the README state-table notes and the generated references. Each is owed by a gate or a convention this record checked; accepted — right.
4. **No Studio form row** (deviation 4): the `externalSharingModel` precedent; a `planned` key is not offered, and the forms-derived i18n bundles therefore stay unchanged. Right.
5. **Second-merge `view.mdx` regeneration** (deviation 5): the net diff against the merge base shows exactly six added rows in `view.mdx` and no other change there, so `main`'s `editInline` default sits in the base and was not dropped. Right.
6. **The open question, the seat's A** (an object's own `listViews`, served inside `/meta/object`, gated by #22639 with the same all-required predicate): correctly answered, not an escalation. The door is a consequence of "same shape" (declaring on `ListViewSchema` alone would fork the shape — B), the ruling says server-enforced and declared is enforced (C would leave a declared, never-enforced key), and the describe's "until the `/meta` read gate applies it" holds for that door because `/meta/object` is a `/meta` read. The veto is open on #22639 (scope note 6096254862). One thing to carry, not a defect here: this changeset's "Not enforced yet" paragraph names the `view` and `dashboard` reads as the enforcing half; #22639's own changeset must name the object read too, or an upgrading author is never told that door was gated.
7. **`validateCapabilityReferences` does not resolve the two new keys** (out-of-scope finding, carried to #22639): acceptable while nothing reads the key — a misspelling hides nothing today and the `authorHint` says so — and the record-block carrier (#18159) is the precedent of a key this lint also skips. Consequence at this head: `capabilities.mdx`'s pre-existing sentence "it resolves every `requiredPermissions` reference" is over-broad by two more carriers; that sentence is not this PR's, and the flip is where it is made true. Carried.
8. **`authorWarn` does not reach named `listViews` entries** (out-of-scope finding): verified in the walk (above); the describe clause covers those doors. Right, nothing to file.
9. **`check:platform-checklist` red** is #22594 and is kept out of per-PR CI by maintainer decision (`lint.yml` says so); no check-run on this head carries it. Right.
10. **PR state for enqueue:** draft, no assignee, `Lint & Repo Gates` and four `Test Core` shards still running at post time (named in ①). The merge-group guard reads this record; the required-status rules read those jobs.

**VERDICT: PASS**
